walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 1: Performing — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 1: Performing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 1: Performing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many crotchets equal a semibreve?
A dot after a note adds?
options: A quarter of its value
A half of its value
A full extra
A double value
Music in 3/4 time.
Three sections: A, contrasting B, and a return to A (ABA).
Three different sections (ABC).
It has only five notes.

mcqs.q: How does D Dorian differ from D minor?
options: Dorian has a raised 6th (B natural) compared to natural minor.
Dorian has no sharps or flats at all.
It has only five notes.
They are the same scale.

mcqs.q: How does a harmonic minor scale differ from a natural minor?
options: All notes are raised by a semitone.
The seventh degree is raised by a semitone (creating a leading note).
Music in 3/4 time.
It has only five notes.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Note value”?
options: Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.
Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.
Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.
Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Dotted note”?
options: Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.
Dot after note increases its duration by half (e.g., dotted crotchet = 1.5 beats).
Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.
Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Crotchet (quarter note)”?
options: Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.
Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.
Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Semibreve (whole note)”?
options: Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.
Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Dot after note increases its duration by half (e.g., dotted crotchet = 1.5 beats).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Rest”?
options: Dot after note increases its duration by half (e.g., dotted crotchet = 1.5 beats).
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.
Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Quaver (eighth note)”?
options: Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.
Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.
